subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals — next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jordan Smith <jordan.smith@zenhealth.com>, Priya Rao <priya.rao@zenhealth.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 30 Jul 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: observability & evals — next steps

Hi Jordan / Priya —

Thanks again for the demo earlier — really helpful to understand ZenHealth's evaluation goals. Quick recap from our side and proposed next steps so we stay aligned: 

Pain points you called out:
- Lack of visibility into per-request/model token cost and tail-latency for multi-tenant inference.
- Difficulty detecting regressions in quality when swapping model variants or updating prompts.
- Need for safe rollout guardrails to avoid user-visible regressions during canary/A-B.

Current stack notes you shared:
- Production app running on Kubernetes (GKE) with a frontend routing layer and an internal ML infra team.
- Using hosted models via vendor X today for prototyping; consider private/dedicated for latency/cost controls.

Success criteria for a successful eval (what you asked to measure):
- Observability: per-route latency P95 <= 350ms, error rate < 0.5%, and cost-per-1000-tokens reduction target vs current baseline.
- Quality: regression alerting when golden-prompt set accuracy drops >3% (or top-N acceptance).
- Rollout: ability to do canary rollouts with automatic rollback on regression or latency SLO breaches.

What we can provide this week:
- Sample observability dashboards (per-route latency, tokens/cost breakdown, model-level KPIs). See attached sample-dashboard.png.
- An "observability playbook" PDF with recommended tracing hooks, request-id mapping, and KV cache visibility (attached redwood-observability-playbook.pdf).
- A starter golden-prompt spreadsheet template to capture your test prompts and acceptance criteria (attached golden-prompts.xlsx).

Suggested next steps:
1) Rishi to share quick notes on tracing hooks and minimal SDK changes to emit request IDs and model/span metadata. (Rishi: can you drop that by EOD?)
2) ZenHealth to populate a small golden prompt set (10-20 examples) and share expected outputs so we can wire up regression alerts.
3) Schedule a 45-min technical walkthrough next week (demoing the dashboards and alerting) — propose Tue 8/3 or Wed 8/4.

If that matches your read, I’ll schedule the walkthrough and loop in our security contact for the SOC2 questionnaire next steps.

Thanks,

Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0123

Marissa —

This is perfect and captures our needs. A couple quick clarifications from Priya and me after internal sync: 
- The latency SLOs you listed look achievable; we'll confirm baseline P95 from our dashboard and share by EOD Monday.
- For quality/regression detection, we'd prefer alerts be tied to both (a) golden prompt acceptance rate and (b) a small human-labeled holdout set to avoid false positives.
- On rollout guardrails: automated rollback on either regression OR if token-cost spikes >20% during canary sounds reasonable.

We’ll start populating the golden-prompt sheet you attached.

To confirm availability: Tue 8/3 10:30–11:15am PT works for our infra + ML lead.

Thanks — Jordan

Hey Jordan / Priya —

Quick technical notes and what's in the attachments: 
- Tracing hooks: we recommend emitting a request_id at the router edge and propagating it into the inference call. Include model name, model_version, route, and prompt_hash as span tags. That allows joining logs -> traces -> per-request token cost.
- KV cache visibility: we can expose KV hit/miss metrics per-user keyspace to help tune cache sizing during evals.
- Dashboards: attached sample-dashboard.png (per-route P50/P95, token breakdown, cost per 1k tokens, model-level throughput). We can add a per-prompt latency heatmap if you can supply sample prompt lengths.
- Golden prompts: golden-prompts.xlsx contains columns: prompt_id, prompt_text, expected_output, acceptance_criteria, reviewer. Use this to drive automated regression checks.
- Regression alerts: suggest two alert types — (1) quality regression on golden prompt acceptance rate drop >3% over rolling 1h, (2) cost/latency breach thresholds during canary. Both can trigger auto-rollback and Slack/email notifications.

Attachments included:
- redwood-observability-playbook.pdf (tracing + instrumentation checklist)
- sample-dashboard.png (mockup)
- golden-prompts.xlsx (template)

Next steps I propose from engineering side:
- We can provide a 1-hour technical walkthrough of the SDK/tracing hooks and dashboard wiring. I can cover the rollout guardrail config.
- If you send 10–20 golden prompts and a small holdout set, we’ll onboard them into our eval pipeline and wire up alerts within 48 business hours.

I’ll drop a short runbook and the minimal SDK patch in a follow-up email.

—Rishi
